title: Lists, dicts and floats - the shapes you handle all course

questions.prompt: The `team` question in cases/routing.json has "criteria": {"billing": "Charges...", "technical": "Errors...", "sales": "Plans...", "other": "None of the above"}. What are the four option names, and why?
options: Charges..., Errors..., Plans..., None of the above - they are the dict's values
billing, technical, sales, other - they are the dict's keys
0, 1, 2, 3 - they are the positions of the keys
The four questions is_billing, team, severity and thresholds
questions.explain: For a choice question the option names are the keys of the criteria dict, and the values are the human-readable descriptions. The first option confuses the vocabulary with the descriptions - and note that the answer's value is the key, e.g. "billing". The third option is wrong because a choice question is unordered by name; only a score question is indexed by position. The fourth option lists unrelated parts of the case file.

questions.prompt: The `severity` question has "criteria": ["No impact", "Minor", "Major", "Critical"] and the provider answers with the value 1.0. What does that mean?
options: The severity is 1 out of 4, i.e. the first level, "No impact"
The probability that the severity is "Minor"
The index into the ordered criteria list, i.e. "Minor"
The number of criteria the model skipped
questions.explain: A score question's criteria is a list, and the answer is the index into it - 1 selects the second level, "Minor". The first option is the trap: reading 1 as "one of four", i.e. the first entry, when the list is zero-based. The score is a position, not a magnitude: the harness compares levels with a half-step tolerance (abs(value - gold) < 0.5), which only makes sense for positions. The second option confuses the value with the probabilities dict, which for a score is keyed by the string form of the index. The fourth describes nothing in the protocol.

questions.prompt: You need the third option of a `choice` question whose criteria is a dict with keys billing, technical, sales, other. Which access is correct?
questions.explain: The option names are keys, so you look one up by name: ["sales"] is the third option. The first option indexes a dict by position and raises a TypeError. The second returns None silently, because .get() with a missing key does not raise - it is the quiet failure mode to watch for. The third would return the description text rather than the name, so it is the wrong string.

questions.prompt: In cases/format_variants.json the same ticket appears as a plain string, as a flat dict, and as a nested dict. Why does the harness care about the difference?
options: Because the shape of the state is itself a variable being measured - it changes the probability the model gives
Because the providers reject a state that is not a string
Because json.load() cannot read a dict at the top level
Because nested states cost more tokens and would break the spend cap
questions.explain: run_format_friction() sends the same content in three serialisations and measures how far the probability moves - that is the format-friction finding this repo is built around, and it needs the state passed through untouched. The second option is wrong because the providers accept any state; JevProvider.decide() puts it straight into the payload. The third option is wrong because json.load() returns whatever the file contains, dicts included - harness.load_cases() relies on that. The fourth option is a half-truth about tokens with no bearing on the spend cap, which is a dollar amount checked between calls.
